title: Tiered Fallback, Fidelity and Crediting Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a standardized approach for defining tiered fallback behavior, fidelity levels, and crediting rules used across Redwood Inference products. It is intended for product managers, SREs, platform engineers, and customer success teams who collaborate on contract negotiation, rollout planning, and operational runbooks.

Purpose:
- Provide a single source of truth for how fidelity tiers map to SLAs, latency expectations, and per-unit credit adjustments.
- Give step-by-step procedures for configuring and rolling out fallback policies for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Define economic crediting rules when a tenant receives lower-fidelity responses or is served by fallback model variants.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to all inference surfaces (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking) exposed by Redwood API and Dedicated pools.
- Covers hosted and Dedicated; on-prem (Private) may apply variants of these rules subject to contract.
- Primary readers: Product, Eng-SRE, Eng-Platform, Customer Success, Sales-engineering.

Key definitions:
1. Fidelity Level: a discrete named configuration of model variant + quantization + sequence-length cap that defines expected output quality and latency. Example names: HIGH, STANDARD, ECONOMY.
2. Fallback Path: the ordered list of model variants and regions to try when the primary model/region cannot meet the target SLOs.
3. Crediting: the compensation applied to customer usage (tokens/requests) when Redwood returns responses at a lower agreed fidelity due to operational conditions.
4. Fidelity Contract: a formal mapping in the customer plan that enumerates guaranteed fidelity per route and the crediting terms for deviations.

Tier mapping (default recommended matrix):
| Fidelity | Model class | Latency SLO (p95) | Typical token cost factor | Credit multiplier | Use cases |
|----------|-------------|-------------------:|--------------------------:|------------------:|-----------|
| HIGH     | LLM-Large fp16 | <= 150 ms | 1.0x | 1.0x | Mission-critical chat, extractive QA |
| STANDARD | LLM-Medium q4_0 | <= 300 ms | 0.6x | 1.1x | Product helpers, lightweight summarization |
| ECONOMY  | LLM-Small q4_0 | <= 700 ms | 0.25x | 1.4x | Bulk embeddings, non-interactive batch jobs |

Notes about the matrix: values are illustrative defaults. Sales and enterprise contracts may substitute numerical SLOs and credit multipliers.

Requirements (must-have):
1. Every customer plan/key must have an explicit Fidelity Contract attached to their tenant profile.
2. Fidelity Contracts must declare: primary fidelity, allowed fallback tiers, and credit multiplier table.
3. The platform must emit telemetry events for each request indicating: requested_fidelity, served_fidelity, fallback_reason (if any), and credit_applied (Y/N + amount).
4. The console billing export must include per-tenant credit adjustments and an auditable reason code.

Design and operational playbook:
A. Pre-deployment: configuring a new Fidelity Contract
  1. PM and Sales model the recommended tier using the matrix above and customer acceptance criteria.
  2. Create a Fidelity Contract object in the contract service with fields: primary_tier, allowed_fallbacks (ordered), credit_table_reference (ID).
  3. Circulate contract summary to Customer Success and Engineering for review.
  4. Add the contract ID to the tenant profile; set flag: fidelity_enforced=true.

B. Runtime behavior: routing and fallback logic
  1. On request arrival, router evaluates tenant fidelity_enforced flag. If false, follow default routing.
  2. Attempt to schedule on primary_tier pool with tenant-specific placement constraints. If queueing time > latency_threshold_for_primary (configurable), trigger fallback.
  3. When fallback triggers, select first allowed_fallback that matches capability and region. Annotate request with served_fidelity and fallback_reason.
  4. If no fallback available, follow graceful degradation policy (see section: Graceful degradation).

C. Crediting calculation and billing pipeline
  1. For every request served at a fidelity lower than contract primary, compute credit = base_charge * (credit_multiplier - 1).
  2. Credits are batched hourly and written to the billing pipeline with reason_code values: {"fallback_capacity", "fallback_region", "degraded_quant", "customer_migration"}.
  3. Customer console shows credits in a separate line item and an explanation linked to the telemetry trace id.

D. Rollout / experiment steps for changing defaults globally
  1. Define experiment hypothesis and target metrics: e.g., 10% cost reduction with <=1% customer impact to fidelity-based satisfaction.
  2. Stage in Canary: 1% of traffic across non-critical routes for 48 hours. Monitor metric set (latency_p95, quality_eval_loss, credit_rate).
  3. Incrementally increase to 10% and 50% with 72-hour holds. If quality regression exceeds threshold or credit_rate spikes unexpectedly, rollback to prior config.
  4. After reaching 100%, publish a change notice and update standard contract language.

Graceful degradation policy (customer-visible levels):
- Level 0: No degradation. Primary fidelity served. No credit.
- Level 1: Regional fallback to equivalent tier. Credit multiplier 1.05x. Visible in console as "temporary regional fallback".
- Level 2: Variant fallback (lower-parameter model or quantized weights). Credit multiplier 1.2x. Prominent console message and email if persistent > 6 hours.
- Level 3: Economy path (batch or rate-limited). Credit multiplier 1.4x and potential partial request latency increase; CS notified immediately for enterprise tenants.

Operational runbook (incident triage steps):
1. Detect: Alert when tenant-level credit_rate per hour > 5% OR fidelity downgrade count > 1% of traffic. Alert target: Eng-SRE + Customer Success.
2. Triage: Identify fallback_reason codes frequency. If due to capacity, check Dedicated pool autoscaling and preemptible inventory.
3. Mitigate: Scale up target pools, widen allowed_fallback region list temporarily, or enable burst capacity for affected tenant.
4. Communicate: Post incident summary to customer-facing status page and create a ticket for CS to reach out to affected customers.
5. Postmortem: Include crediting volumes, root cause, and proposed adjustments to the Fidelity Contract if recurring.

Metrics and telemetry (required):
- fidelity_served_count (per tier)
- fallback_invocations (per reason_code)
- credits_issued_amount (currency)
- quality_regressions_by_promptset (link to eval harness id)
- customer_satisfaction_impacted (CSAT delta correlated to fidelity events)

Ownership and SLAs:
- Product: sets default matrices and contract language; approves changes to credit multipliers.
- Eng-Platform: implements Fidelity Contract storage and runtime enforcement.
- Eng-SRE: integrates alerting, autoscaling, and runbooks.
- Customer Success: owns customer communication and compensation workflows.

Template: Fidelity Contract (human-readable summary)
- Tenant: <tenant-name>
- Primary Fidelity: <HIGH|STANDARD|ECONOMY>
- Allowed Fallbacks (ordered): [STANDARD, ECONOMY]
- Credit Multipliers: HIGH->STANDARD:1.1x, HIGH->ECONOMY:1.4x
- Notification threshold: >6 hours continuous downgrade triggers email

FAQ:
Q: When do we waive credits for trial tenants?
A: Trials under 30 days receive one-time grace credit for persistent fidelity regression > 12 hours; otherwise standard credit policy applies.

Q: Can customers opt out of automatic fallback?
A: Yes. A flag (allow_fallback=false) can be set in the Fidelity Contract. Customers who opt out may experience higher error rates and will not receive credits for failures.

Appendix: Example CLI snippets
- View Fidelity Contract for tenant:
  rwdctl contracts get --tenant tenant-1234 --format yaml

- Force a temporary fallback allowance for tenant (emergency):
  rwdctl contracts patch --tenant tenant-1234 --set allow_fallback=true --set allowed_fallbacks=["STANDARD","ECONOMY"]
